title: Chili Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Chili Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Chili nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and calcium in sili, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Chili nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your sili (chili) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, boron, zinc, sulfur and manganese. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Close view of chili leaves turned pale yellow green from nitrogen shortage
heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium, boron, zinc, sulfur and manganese stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which chili nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a chili nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest chili nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in chili

blocks.alt: Close view of chili leaves turned pale yellow green from nitrogen shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Older leaves turn pale to light green and then yellow evenly, veins included. Plants branch less and stay short, leaves are small, and fruits are small and pale. In severe cases lower leaves yellow and drop early. You see it most at this stage: from early growth through fruiting.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in sili
Sandy soils, heavy rain or watering, low organic matter and long gaps between side dressings.
How to tell it apart
Sulfur shortage starts on the young leaves. Magnesium shortage keeps veins green on old leaves. To be sure, check that the bottom leaves yellow first, then do a soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Side dress with urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test. For a quick fix, try a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days. Side dress 5 to 10 grams of Urea 46 0 0 a plant, about 1 to 2 bags per hectare, every two to three weeks from flowering, and water it in.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Crown Champion Ammonium Sulfate** by Aqua Hydroponic Prime Ventures (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Amigo Planters Sabic Zinc Coated Urea** by La Filipina (46 0 0 with 0.1 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add compost at planting and split nitrogen into several side dressings.
Potassium deficiency in chili

blocks.alt: Chili pepper leaf seen from below with brown scorched patches along the tip and edges, from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Çetindağ et al., Pepper Nutrient Deficiency Dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: Leaf tips burn and dead patches appear between the veins, starting on older leaves. Leaves crinkle and curl, become fewer and smaller, and the plant is stunted. Yellowing from potassium shortage does not recover even after feeding, so act early. You see it most at this stage: fruiting, when fruits draw potassium from the leaves.
Why potassium deficiency happens in sili
Sandy or acid soils, heavy rain that leaches potassium, and fertilizer programs with little potash.
How to tell it apart
Salt or fertilizer burn also scorches tips. Check if fertilizer was placed too close to the stem. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For immediate relief, try a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) with a sticker. Lime acid soil to keep pH above 6. A usual dose is 1 to 2 bags of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 per hectare, split from flowering to fruit fill.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash at planting and again at flowering and fruiting. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Calcium deficiency in chili

blocks.alt: Long pepper fruit with a brown, shrunken, rotting tip from calcium shortage (blossom end rot)
blocks.caption: Photo: Metin GULESCI, Leaf Tobacco, Bugwood.org, CC BY 3.0 US, via ipmimages.org

blocks.text: Sunken, water soaked spots form near the tip (blossom end) of the fruit, then harden, dry and turn black. Mould may grow on them. Young leaves curl upward, are small and deformed, and their edges yellow then die. Root and shoot tips can brown and die, and flower buds may fail. You see it most at this stage: flowering and early fruit growth, in hot dry spells.
Why calcium deficiency happens in sili
Uneven watering and dry spells, acid sandy soils, salty soils, and heavy nitrogen or potassium. Boron shortage and high phosphorus can add to it.
How to tell it apart

Sunscald makes pale papery patches on the sun side of the fruit, not at the tip. Fruit rots from disease spread fast and are soft from the start. To be sure, look for the spots at the tip end of young fruits after dry weather, then do a soil test for calcium and pH.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

Water evenly and mulch. On acid soil, lime by the soil test: usually 1 to 3 tons of Agricultural lime or Dolomite per hectare, mixed in 2 to 4 weeks before planting. Gypsum on soil that is not acid. Remove affected fruits.

Sold here with calcium: **Micronized Activated Calcite** by CMCS Agricultural Products (37.6 percent calcium), **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Titon Pro** by Vast Agro (27.2 percent calcium, 6.1 percent silicon and 3.6 percent magnesium) and **Crown Champion Nitrogen Calcium Compound (Cal Nit)** by Aqua Hydroponic Prime Ventures (15 0 0 with 18 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soil before planting, keep the soil evenly moist, and avoid heavy ammonium fertilizer. Keep potash in balance with magnesium and calcium.
Phosphorus deficiency in chili

Stems, leaf stalks and the undersides of leaves turn purple. In severe cases leaves get a blue grey sheen. Plants have fewer leaves, short thin shoots, few branches and weak roots. Flowering and ripening come late and fruits are small and distorted. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in sili
Acid or iron rich soils, low organic matter, cold or waterlogged soils.
How to tell it apart
Cool nights can turn seedlings purple for a short time. Nitrogen shortage gives pale rather than purple leaves. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply the recommended phosphorus near the roots based on the soil test. Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term. Keep soil near pH 6.2 to 7.0. A usual basal dose is 4 to 6 bags of Complete 14 14 14 per hectare, 10 to 20 grams a hill, mixed into the soil at transplanting.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a phosphorus starter at transplanting and add compost.
Magnesium deficiency in chili

blocks.alt: Chili pepper leaf on white paper turning yellow between the veins while the main veins stay green, from magnesium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Çetindağ et al., Pepper Nutrient Deficiency Dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: Leaves that have just reached full size, and older leaves, turn yellow between the veins while the largest veins stay green. Dead spots form in the yellow areas, leaves drop early and yield falls. You see it most at this stage: fruiting.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in sili
Sandy acid soils, heavy rain, and heavy potash or ammonium fertilizer.
How to tell it apart
Manganese and iron shortage start on the young top leaves, where even small veins stay green. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and potassium, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Try magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare. Do not apply magnesium and potassium fertilizer together. Put the soil dose in before planting or when the rains begin. Sprays show results in 10 to 14 days.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soil. Test the soil every two or three years. Lime acid soil with Dolomite rather than plain lime.
Boron deficiency in chili

New leaves are pale, misshapen, brittle and small, and the plant loses its main tip and grows bushy. Fruits stay small and light, crack, and drop before they mature. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit set.
Why boron deficiency happens in sili
Sandy soils where boron leaches, heavily limed or alkaline soils, low organic matter and drought.
How to tell it apart

Virus diseases also twist new leaves. Check for insects such as thrips and mites, and whether the pattern follows soil patches. To be sure, soil test for boron and a leaf tissue test. In a soil test, less than 0.5 ppm of boron is low.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Try borax in the soil at about 10 kg per hectare or a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water (16 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Peppers need only a little boron, so do not repeat doses without a test. Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizer. Give boron before flowering: flowers and fruit set need it most.

Sold here with boron: **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl Chem (11 percent boron), **Fertibagra 15G** by Unilox Far East Resources (14.6 percent boron), **B17 (Boric Acid)** by Newman Chemicals (17 percent boron) and **Better Yield** by Bacphil Planters Fertilizer (0 0 0.9 with 10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use boron only where tests show low levels, and keep organic matter up. Test the soil every two or three years.
Zinc deficiency in chili

Young leaves yellow between the veins and can turn whitish. Leaves are small, stiff and brittle, stems are thin, and the space between leaves is short. The crop matures unevenly. You see it most at this stage: vegetative growth and early flowering.
Why zinc deficiency happens in sili
High pH or overlimed soil, heavy phosphorus fertilizer, waterlogged soil.
How to tell it apart

Leaf curl virus also makes small, crinkled leaves, but it comes with whiteflies on the plants. Zinc shortage shows yellowing between the veins over a whole soil patch. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf tissue test. In a soil test, less than 0.8 ppm of zinc is low.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Try zinc sulfate in the soil at about 20 kg per hectare. In severe cases a morning spray of zinc sulfate at 2 grams plus calcium carbonate at 2.5 grams per liter of water (40 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Do not apply zinc and phosphate together. Give the soil dose at planting or when the rains begin, and sprays on young growth.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc), **Semia** by SCL Filipinas (20 percent zinc) and **Omex Zynergy** by Jardine Distribution (3.8 percent zinc and 2.1 percent copper). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep soil pH between 5 and 7.5 and avoid excess phosphorus. Test the soil every two or three years.
Sulfur deficiency in chili

Young leaves turn pale then yellow overall, with reddish veins and leaf stalks. Leaves are small, brittle and twisted and curl downward, and growth is held back. You see it most at this stage: early growth on light soils.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in sili
Sandy, low organic matter soils and fertilizer programs with no sulfur.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage starts at the bottom leaves. To be sure, soil test for sulfate and a leaf tissue test. In a soil test, less than 10 ppm of sulfate sulfur is low.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency

Use ammonium sulfate or other sulfur containing fertilizer. Try sulfur dust at about 25 kg per hectare on sulfur deficient soil, and gypsum on alkaline soil. Give it at planting or with the first side dress.

Sold here with sulfur: **Crown Champion Ammonium Sulfate** by Aqua Hydroponic Prime Ventures (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur), **Philphos Gypsum** (22.2 percent calcium and 17.4 percent sulfur), **Harvester Sulphate of Potash** by Universal Harvester (0 0 50 with 17.5 percent sulfur) and **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include ammonium sulfate in the program and add organic matter. Do not burn crop residues. Test the soil every two or three years.
Manganese deficiency in chili

Leaves that are nearly full size show mottled yellowing between the veins. So a thin net of green veins stands out on the pale green blade. Young leaves yellow at the edges and dark dead areas form along the veins. Fruits may show raised dark brown to black spots. You see it most at this stage: vegetative growth and fruiting.
Why manganese deficiency happens in sili
High pH or overlimed soils, sandy soils, and cold wet spells.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage starts on old leaves. Iron shortage gives a clean yellow without dark spots. To be sure, soil pH test and a leaf tissue test. In a soil test, less than 1 ppm of manganese is low.
What to apply for manganese deficiency

Try a manganese sulfate spray at 2 grams per liter of water (32 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) after a soil test confirms the need. Spray the young leaves in the cool of the day, soon after sunrise or near sunset.

Sold here with manganese: **Manganese Sulfate** by Zetryl Chem (31 percent manganese), **Turan** by SCL Filipinas (11 percent manganese, 6 percent zinc and 2.8 percent copper), **Tierramino MN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 12 percent manganese) and **Multimate** by Agway (4 0 0 with 4.5 percent sulfur, 2.8 percent zinc and 1.8 percent manganese). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [manganese deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/manganese-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not overlime. Keep soil pH near 6 to 6.5.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any chili nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your sili needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Chili nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my sili leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: lower leaves turn pale yellow, veins included, and plants branch little. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in chili?
items.a: Side dress with urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test. For a quick fix, try a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in chili?
items.a: Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For immediate relief, try a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) with a sticker.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes calcium deficiency in chili?
items.a: Water evenly and mulch. On acid soil, lime by the soil test: usually 1 to 3 tons of Agricultural lime or Dolomite per hectare, mixed in 2 to 4 weeks before planting.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my sili lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the chili nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
